summary.headline: robots.txt disallows every major AI agent's direct-fetch and training crawlers with no stated rationale, while the newer '-SearchBot' variants of the same companies are not named at all and fall through to the permissive default — critical severity, Confirm whether blocking every named retrieval agent's direct-fetch/user-request crawler is a deliberate anti-scraping decision; if so, extend it consistently to the newer '-SearchBot' agent names too, and consider stating the rationale in the file the way other large sites do.

findings.title: robots.txt disallows every major AI agent's direct-fetch and training crawlers with no stated rationale, while the newer '-SearchBot' variants of the same companies are not named at all and fall through to the permissive default
findings.evidence: robots.txt names GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, and Amazonbot in a single group with 'Disallow: /' and no explanatory comment anywhere in the file (unlike sites in this audit's other reports that state an explicit rationale). OAI-SearchBot and Claude-SearchBot -- the newer, search-indexing-specific agents from the same two companies whose other agents are blocked -- are not named in any group and fall through to the permissive 'User-agent: *' block, which carries no blanket disallow. Verified directly: OAI-SearchBot and Claude-SearchBot resolve 'allowed' on a product path while GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User all resolve 'disallowed' on the same path. This is the same pattern this audit has flagged on other sites as evidence of an incomplete, boilerplate agent list rather than a considered policy -- here it blocks not just training agents (a defensible choice on its own) but every live-request/user-initiated retrieval agent by name (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User), while missing the newest agent names.

reproduction.observed: A single group naming GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Amazonbot with Disallow: / and no comment; OAI-SearchBot and Claude-SearchBot absent from the file entirely
reproduction.expected: Either a stated rationale for blocking live-request retrieval agents specifically, or the newer SearchBot-style agents treated consistently with the ones already named

suggested_action.summary: Confirm whether blocking every named retrieval agent's direct-fetch/user-request crawler is a deliberate anti-scraping decision; if so, extend it consistently to the newer '-SearchBot' agent names too, and consider stating the rationale in the file the way other large sites do.
suggested_action.mechanism: As written, an assistant fetching a specific product page on a user's behalf (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User) is blocked by name, while the same companies' separate search-indexing crawlers are not -- an inconsistency that suggests the list was assembled once and not revisited as agent names changed, rather than a considered current policy.
steps: Decide whether blocking live user-request retrieval agents specifically (as opposed to training-only agents) is the intended policy.
If it is not, remove ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User from the blocked group.
If it is, add OAI-SearchBot and Claude-SearchBot to the same group for consistency.
suggested_action.verification: The treatment of a company's live-request agent and its search-indexing agent match for every operator named in the file.

findings.title: Search and category-browsing entry points redirect to a bot-verification wall for automated-looking traffic, while the homepage and static content pages remain open
findings.evidence: A plain request to a search results URL (listado.mercadolibre.com.mx/<term>) returns HTTP 302 to /gz/account-verification -- a verification wall, not the search results. The same pattern occurred on a category subdomain (autos.mercadolibre.com.mx). By contrast, the homepage and all 14 sampled static/help/glossary pages returned clean HTTP 200 responses with real content, both to a plain request and (separately, for the homepage) to a full headless-browser render. Since search and category browsing are the primary way a visitor -- or an assistant trying to find a specific product -- would ever reach an individual listing, and the homepage itself does not link to individual product pages in its own markup, this leaves no read-only, guardrail-respecting path from any of this audit's sampled entry points to the site's core content (individual product listings). This audit could not reach a single product page as a result; see not_assessed for what that leaves unverified.

reproduction.expected: 200 with real search results, matching the behavior of the homepage and static pages

suggested_action.summary: Verify whether search and category-browsing pages are intended to be fully gated for all non-session traffic, or whether the verification threshold is unintentionally broader than intended for the site's primary content-discovery paths.
suggested_action.mechanism: If reaching any individual listing requires passing this wall first, no retrieval agent -- however well-behaved -- can answer a question about a specific product without a prior authenticated or verified session, which is a much stronger restriction than the robots.txt-level agent blocks alone would suggest.
steps: Confirm the verification wall's trigger conditions for search and category paths specifically.
If unintentional, scope the wall more narrowly (e.g. to genuinely high-volume automated query patterns) so a single, well-paced request reaches real results.
suggested_action.verification: A single, isolated, well-paced request to a search or category URL returns real results rather than a verification redirect.

not_assessed.check: Structured data (AggregateRating/Review/Product/Offer), answerability, freshness, and engagement on individual product pages
not_assessed.reason: No individual product page was reachable from any of this audit's entry points within its read-only, guardrail-respecting constraints: the homepage does not link to individual listings in its own markup, and both search and category browsing redirect to a bot-verification wall (see the crawl-access findings). No workaround or verification-bypass was attempted, consistent with this audit's guardrails.
not_assessed.impact: This audit cannot say whether MercadoLibre's product pages carry good Product/Offer/AggregateRating markup, quotable descriptions, or a good on-site experience -- only that no path tried could reach one to check. This was the specific mechanism this audit run set out to test (review/rating schema at e-commerce scale) and it could not be completed for this site.

not_assessed.check: Off-site corroboration and entity ambiguity (freshness-corroboration-audit, checks 4-5)
not_assessed.reason: Not performed in this run to stay within the demonstration's time budget.
not_assessed.impact: Not a meaningful concern for an entity as well-known as MercadoLibre across Latin America, but genuinely not checked.
